title: Shortcut Conflict shown when there's no documented conflict.

judgment.rationale: The activation chord works on Windows 11 but Settings reports a system conflict for the historically assigned Win+Shift+C chord, supporting a stale catalog applicability fix.
evidence: The reporter confirms the warning on 0.101.2362 and Windows 11 build 26200 while Color Picker activation works.
A maintainer states Win+Shift+C was historical Cortana/Charms behavior and is generally deprecated on modern Windows 11.
The conflict system is implemented by GlobalHotkeyConflictManager and HotkeyConflictInfo.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve an OS-applicability design while requesting confirmation of the actual catalog entry and supported-version policy.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix covers the stale system-shortcut applicability decision.

proposed_fixes.title: Exclude obsolete Win+Shift+C from current Windows system conflicts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Likely: conflict metadata treats the historical Cortana/Charms chord as current without an OS applicability condition.
plan: Locate the entry that emits the system conflict and verify that it represents Win+Shift+C rather than Win+C or Win+Ctrl+C.
Add supported-version applicability to that entry, excluding it where Windows no longer reserves the chord.
Keep active system and module conflicts unchanged and add positive and negative matcher coverage.
verification: On Windows 11 configure Color Picker as Win+Shift+C and confirm no system-conflict warning while activation works.
Confirm known current system conflicts still appear and validate any supported older Windows behavior.

confidence.rationale: The user result and maintainer history isolate obsolete metadata, but the exact catalog entry and version policy need source confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Color Picker works with Win+Shift+C on Windows 11, but Settings reports an undocumented system shortcut conflict.
known_information: The reporter reproduced on 0.101.2362 stable and Windows 11 build 26200.
The shortcut still activates Color Picker.
Maintainer discussion identifies historical Cortana or Charms ownership.
Settings has GlobalHotkeyConflictManager and HotkeyConflictInfo conflict surfaces.
inferences: The warning likely comes from stale system-conflict metadata rather than hotkey registration.
Version gating is safer than hiding the conflict for Color Picker alone.
issue_context.analysis: The visible warning is incorrect on the reporter's current OS, but the code entry and its compatibility policy must be confirmed before changing shared conflict behavior.
initial_investigation: Read the issue and maintainer clarification.
Located the Settings conflict manager and conflict metadata types.

information_gaps.information: The exact conflict-catalog entry and its intended supported Windows versions
information_gaps.why_needed: It distinguishes an obsolete Win+Shift+C entry from key normalization and prevents suppressing a valid conflict on a supported OS.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Inspect the system shortcut catalog and run its matcher for Win+Shift+C, Win+C, and Win+Ctrl+C on supported Windows versions; record the intended compatibility policy.

design.root_cause: Unconfirmed but likely stale system-shortcut metadata that lacks current-Windows applicability.
evidence: [Observed] Win+Shift+C activates Color Picker despite the warning.
[Observed] A maintainer describes the chord as legacy Cortana/Charms behavior.
[Observed] Shared Settings conflict-manager and metadata types own the warning.
[Inferred] The exact catalog entry needs OS-aware filtering.

affected_files.purpose: Initializes and publishes shortcut conflict results.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The source conflict is surfaced without a confirmed current-OS applicability condition.
implementation_steps.change: Represent supported Windows applicability on the proven Win+Shift+C entry.
edge_cases: Do not collapse Shift/Ctrl modifiers during matching.
Preserve any still-supported legacy Windows behavior.
tests: Matcher tests for Win+Shift+C exclusion and known current conflicts.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Manager publishes conflict metadata to Settings.
implementation_steps.change: Filter only entries outside their declared OS applicability before the UI receives them.
tests: Service test that an inactive system entry does not reach Settings.

verify: On Windows 11 verify the warning disappears and Color Picker continues to activate.
risks: Incorrect version detection could hide a real conflict.
A Color Picker-specific suppression would leave shared metadata wrong.
alternatives: Change only the help link; rejected because the false warning remains.
Suppress all Win+C-family conflicts; rejected because modifier distinctions matter.

adversary.verdict: No blocking objection to the conditional catalog design; exact entry and version policy must be confirmed.
adversary.notes: Do not implement a Color Picker-only suppression.

comment.body: The working Win+Shift+C activation on Windows 11 and the historical Cortana/Charms context point to an obsolete system-conflict entry, not a Color Picker registration failure. Please verify the catalog entry for Win+Shift+C separately from Win+C and Win+Ctrl+C, then confirm the Windows versions on which it should remain a real conflict; that evidence will keep the shared matcher from hiding valid warnings.
